title: Efficient Minimal Polynomial Reduction for Sparse Matrices
description: Formalizes efficient minimal polynomial reduction for structured sparse matrices. For nilpotent M (M^k = 0), reduction can bypass minpoly computation entirely by using X^k as the modulus — degree truncation in O(deg p) work. For upper triangular M, minpoly divides the diagonal product ∏(X - M_i_i), giving an O(n)-computable degree bound. Extends OQ-01 (charpoly efficiency) to the minimal polynomial setting.

meta.author: researcher-5
meta.assumptions: No axioms, no sorries. All 9 theorems fully proved. Key techniques: modByMonic_add_div for reduction; minpoly.dvd + Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd for divisibility; Matrix.charpoly_of_upperTriangular for the triangular case.

overview.historicalContext: Krylov subspace methods (Lanczos, GMRES, Wiedemann) exploit that sparse matrices have small effective minimal polynomial degree. For a nilpotent matrix M of nilpotency index k, the minimal polynomial is X^k — computable in O(1) operations once k is known. This makes the polynomial reduction p %ₘ minpoly(M) equivalent to p %ₘ X^k, which is just degree truncation. For structured sparse matrices in practice (banded, block triangular, nearly nilpotent), this gives dramatic speedups over general O(n³) charpoly computation.
overview.problemStatement: Can the minimal polynomial reduction — evaluating p at M as aeval M (p %ₘ minpoly K M) — be made computationally efficient for sparse matrices? Specifically: (1) For nilpotent M with M^k = 0, can we avoid computing minpoly explicitly? (2) For upper triangular M, what is the degree of minpoly? (3) Does the efficiency of OQ-01 (charpoly reduction) extend to the minpoly setting?
overview.proofStrategy: Three mechanisms: (1) Nilpotent: show minpoly K M | X^k via minpoly.dvd applied to aeval M (X^k) = M^k = 0. Then prove aeval M p = aeval M (p %ₘ X^k) via modByMonic_add_div. This bypasses minpoly entirely. (2) Upper triangular: use charpoly_of_upperTriangular to get charpoly = ∏(X - d_i), then minpoly.dvd gives minpoly | ∏(X - d_i). (3) General: prove the standard reduction aeval M p = aeval M (p %ₘ minpoly K M) using aeval M (minpoly K M) = 0.
keyInsights: For nilpotent M (M^k = 0), X^k can serve as the reduction modulus directly, since minpoly K M | X^k. This avoids computing minpoly altogether — the reduction is just polynomial degree truncation.
The nilpotency index k gives a tight degree bound: deg(minpoly) ≤ k ≤ n. For sparse structured matrices with small k, this is much better than the general bound n.
For upper triangular matrices, minpoly K M divides ∏ᵢ(X - M i i), which is computed in O(n) time by reading the diagonal — matching the efficiency of OQ-01's charpoly approach.

The theorem nilpotent_power_eq_zero — that M^j = 0 for all j ≥ k — is the Lean certificate for Krylov sequence termination. In iterative solvers, the Krylov sequence (v, Mv, M²v, ...) collapses to zero after k steps for nilpotent M, linking the algebraic degree bound to the algorithmic iteration count in Wiedemann's sparse matrix algorithm.
prerequisites: Minimal polynomial theory: minpoly.dvd, minpoly.monic, minpoly.aeval

sections.title: Module Header, Imports, and Setup
sections.summary: Module comment framing the three efficiency mechanisms: nilpotent X^k bypass, upper triangular diagonal product bound, and general minpoly reduction. Imports for Mathlib charpoly/minpoly, polynomial Euclidean division, and nilpotent theory.

sections.title: Part I: Nilpotent Minimal Polynomial Theory
sections.summary: Two theorems: nilpotent_minpoly_dvd_pow (minpoly K M ∣ X^k when M^k = 0, via minpoly.dvd) and nilpotent_minpoly_natDegree_le (deg(minpoly) ≤ k, via natDegree_le_of_dvd). The nilpotency index k provides a tight, O(1)-computable degree bound.

sections.title: Part II: Efficient Polynomial Reduction via Nilpotency
sections.summary: Three theorems: nilpotent_poly_reduction (aeval M p = aeval M (p mod X^k) — the key efficiency result using modByMonic_add_div), nilpotent_power_eq_zero (M^j = 0 for all j ≥ k — Krylov termination certificate), and nilpotent_reduction_equiv (both X^k and minpoly reduction routes agree).

sections.title: Part III: Upper Triangular Minimal Polynomial Bound
sections.summary: Two theorems for upper triangular M: upper_tri_minpoly_dvd_prod (minpoly K M ∣ ∏ᵢ(X − M i i) via charpoly_of_upperTriangular) and upper_tri_minpoly_natDegree_le (deg(minpoly) ≤ n). The diagonal product is O(n) to compute.

sections.title: Part IV: General Reduction, Degree Bound, and Summary
sections.summary: General reduction (minpoly_poly_reduction: aeval M p = aeval M (p mod minpoly K M) for any matrix), degree bound (nilpotent_reduction_degree_lt: deg(p mod X^k) < k), and closing summary comment reviewing all 9 theorems.

conclusion.summary: Nine theorems fully formalize that minimal polynomial reduction is computationally efficient for three classes of structured matrices: nilpotent (X^k bypass, zero minpoly computation), upper triangular (O(n) diagonal product bound), and general (valid reduction for any matrix). The nilpotent case is the most dramatic: reduction degrades to polynomial degree truncation at cost O(deg p).
conclusion.implications: These results connect formal verification directly to practical numerical linear algebra. Krylov subspace methods (Lanczos, Conjugate Gradient, Wiedemann's sparse matrix algorithm over finite fields) exploit exactly these degree bounds — the minimal polynomial degree determines the number of iterations. The formal proof that M^j = 0 for all j ≥ k is the Lean certificate that Krylov sequences terminate in k steps. For a strictly upper triangular n×n matrix (common in elimination algorithms), the nilpotency index is exactly n, so these bounds are tight and the efficiency gain is real.
openQuestions: For a general sparse matrix with sparsity pattern (bandwidth b, or block structure), is there a polynomial-time algorithm to compute a tight degree bound for minpoly that can be formalized in Lean 4?
Can Wiedemann's algorithm for sparse linear systems over finite fields be formalized end-to-end in Lean 4, building on these nilpotent_poly_reduction and upper_tri_minpoly_dvd_prod theorems?

crossReferences.description: OQ-01 proves charpoly efficiency for sparse matrices. OQ-01-OQ-02 extends to the minimal polynomial, showing it is often more efficient still (smaller degree bound, X^k bypass for nilpotent case).
Vector minimal polynomial theory (minpoly.dvd and related). The nilpotent_poly_reduction theorem enables the Krylov termination in OQ-03-OQ-01 for nilpotent matrices.
